title: Boil-water advisory
summary: What to do when the tap may not be safe. In January 2025, Richmond's water plant failure hit Henrico.

sources.title: CDC: Drinking Water Advisories, An Overview
WTVR: Richmond water crisis impacted Henrico and Hanover (Jan 12, 2025)

items.text: Keep stored drinking water, and a way to boil it.
items.note: In January 2025, Richmond's water plant went down (the article blames a power transfer failure). A boil advisory covered Henrico, Hanover and Richmond, and Henrico reported about 24,000 residents without running water at one point.

items.text: Keep a bottle of plain unscented bleach.
Learn the three advisory types: **boil**, **do not drink** and **do not use**.
Bring tap water to a **rolling boil for 1 minute**, then let it cool.
items.note: Boiling kills germs. It does **not** remove chemicals.

items.text: Use bottled or boiled water for drinking, cooking, food prep, baby formula and brushing teeth.
Do not drink water or ice from the fridge or freezer dispensers.
Give pets bottled water or cooled boiled water.
Dishes: use disposable ones if you can.
items.note: A dishwasher is fine with a sanitizing cycle or a final rinse of at least 150°F. By hand, soak rinsed dishes for at least 1 minute in 1 teaspoon of unscented bleach per gallon of water, then air dry.

items.text: Handwashing with tap water and soap is often fine. Bathe without swallowing the water, and sponge-bathe babies and young children.
If it is a **do not drink** advisory: boiling does not help. Use bottled water.
items.note: The contamination is chemical or toxic.

items.text: If it is a **do not use** advisory: use bottled water for everything.
items.note: Do not use the tap in any way. Skin, lung or eye contact may be dangerous.

items.text: If the water stays off or unsafe for long, think about going to Gram's.
Follow your water utility's and local officials' instructions on when tap water is safe again.
